The two new source questions concern the semantics after successful admission.

Cliff adapter maps typed geological structure to native uniform vectors; the current test now references committed baked maps instead of generating textures.

conditional_findings.classification: New95e source-derived contact-surface interpolation and precision policy question; no runtime or restored checkpoint3821 finding.
conditional_findings.canonical_owner: SceneTerrain physical support surface and the explicit precision/interpolation contract of the contact heightmap consumers.
conditional_findings.first_failed_contract: The shared raster records support at grid vertices, while the bark shader interpolates using the opposite cell diagonal from sampled SceneTerrain and the weather shader uses bilinear interpolation.
conditional_findings.trace: For a symbolic2x2, 1m-spaced sampled SceneTerrain with row-major heights [0,0,0,1]m, the admitted grid has finite heights and nonzero finite normals. At scene point (-0.25,-0.25)m, the CPU support query has cell fraction (0.25,0.25); its x+y<=1 triangle yields0m. A contact image whose four vertex support queries succeed encodes the minimum and maximum exactly as0 and65535. At the same point, the bark shader uses x>=y and the x0y0-to-x1y1 diagonal, yielding0.25m; the weather shader bilinear expression yields0.0625m. The weather material receives the contact range and image only for a non-clear, nonzero-intensity active weather scene; tree residency caches the same type of image/range and bark material supplies those bounds.
conditional_findings.safeguards: The arithmetic compares selected source expressions and a symbolically constructor-admissible grid; no grid, support query, image, material, texture, shader, scene or GPU was executed. The scene producer, tree fragments, actual weather location and rendering were not observed. It is not established that weather interpolation must match physical triangles, that this specific grid is a supported generated scene, or that any visual effect is perceptible. Native texture interpretation and coordinate transforms remain policy and integration dependencies.
dependencies: Decide which consumers require the exact physical support triangle and which may intentionally use a smoothed visual approximation.

Reconcile related support precision, tree contact caching and shader findings only when exact aliases are established.
acceptance_requirements: The contact interpolation contract explicitly matches required support geometry or documents and bounds each intended visual approximation.
Preserve admitted flat and sloped surfaces, vertex boundaries, tree contact behavior and precipitation behavior without moving tactical collision authority to persistent storage.
conditional_findings.discovery: partial; a source-level admitted-grid arithmetic discrepancy and bounded consumers traced, supported producers and accuracy policy open

conditional_findings.classification: New95e source-derived narrow-range encoding/decoding policy question; no runtime or restored checkpoint3821 finding.
conditional_findings.canonical_owner: TerrainContactHeightmap image and the matched range supplied to each decoder.
conditional_findings.first_failed_contract: The encoder normalizes elevations using max(actual span,0.001m), but it returns the original minimum and maximum to shaders that decode using their difference.
conditional_findings.trace: For a symbolic2x2 1m-spaced finite sampled terrain with row-major heights [0,0,0,1/2048]m, the actual range is0 to0.00048828125m. The encoder divides its maximum by approximately0.001 before 16-bit quantization; the returned range still ends at0.00048828125m. Both inspected shaders decode that value by mixing the original minimum and maximum, giving roughly0.000238m at the maximum texel, rather than the original0.000488m. This is a source-level scale mismatch, separate from the interpolation diagonal question; the error is below0.00025m in this illustrative range.
conditional_findings.safeguards: No terrain, constructor, support query, image, shader, GPU or product was run. Flat zero-span terrain remains legitimate and needs a defined denominator; actual producer distribution, supported elevation resolution and whether the sub-millimetre difference matters are unproved. This does not assert a gameplay or visible defect.
dependencies: Establish intended encoding error and visual tolerance across flat, narrow and ordinary ranges and across all image consumers.
Keep the represented decode range and normalized encoder span coherent if accuracy policy requires it; separately retain true physical bounds where they serve other purposes.
Trace all consumers and aliases without merging this scale mismatch with independent interpolation and retained-scene identity questions.
acceptance_requirements: For supported terrain ranges, the image decoder and encoder agree on the representation or document a bounded tolerated deviation.
Preserve a well-defined flat-terrain representation and distinguish physical bounds from an expanded encoding range if both are needed.
conditional_findings.discovery: partial; mismatch and symbolic bounded example traced, supported resolution and all consumers open
